brief.conference_theme: The future we fund: who is shaping the new era of philanthropy

plan.summary: Find nationally recognized philanthropy leaders suited to a keynote on who is shaping philanthropy’s future, prioritizing people with documented conference or public presentation experience. Medium budget favors established experts and select headliners; New Haven is the event location, but the search can be national.

angles: Yale philanthropy faculty and researchers at Yale School of Management’s Program on Social Enterprise and Innovation
Philanthropy scholars who have presented at Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations and Voluntary Action (ARNOVA) conferences
CEOs and program leaders at national foundations such as Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, and Hewlett Foundation with conference keynote records
Philanthropy leaders featured as speakers at Council on Foundations conferences or the GEO National Conference
Researchers and policy leaders at Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy who present at national philanthropy convenings
Philanthropy policy experts at Independent Sector and the National Committee for Responsive Philanthropy with documented speaking appearances
Founders of major philanthropic initiatives and giving platforms featured at the Skoll World Forum or Aspen Ideas Festival
Leaders of donor-advised fund and impact-investing organizations who speak at SOCAP or the Milken Institute Global Conference
Leaders of community-centered philanthropy and grassroots grantmaking organizations speaking at the Grantmakers for Effective Organizations National Conference
Foundation and philanthropy equity advocates at the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity and the United Philanthropy Forum conference
National philanthropy reporters and editors at The Chronicle of Philanthropy and Inside Philanthropy who moderate public events
Authors and podcast hosts covering philanthropy who have presented at Aspen Ideas Festival or the Council on Foundations conference

cards.name: Una Osili
cards.job_title: Efroymson Chair in Philanthropy; Associate Dean for Research and International Programs
cards.organization: Indiana University Lilly Family School of Philanthropy
cards.could_speak_on: How demographic shifts, changing social norms, and global giving patterns are reshaping the philanthropic landscape and its next era.
talk_ideas: What current giving trends reveal about philanthropy’s future
How demographic and social changes are altering charitable giving
Global philanthropy and the institutions shaping it
cards.bio: Una Osili is a global philanthropy and social innovation expert at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, where she holds the Efroymson Chair and serves as Associate Dean for Research and International Programs. Her work includes research on Giving USA and global philanthropy indexes and tracking.
credentials: PhD; the profile describes her as an internationally recognized expert in philanthropy, economics, and international development
cards.why_fit: Her research and public-facing work on U.S. and global giving trends directly support a keynote about who is shaping philanthropy’s next era.

past_speaking.event: CGP Conference 2024 closing keynote
Giving USA 2024 presentation and panel
The Fund Raising School First Day podcast on philanthropy during crises

notable_work: Research and publication of Giving USA, the annual report on American philanthropy
Global Philanthropy Environment Index and Global Philanthropy Tracker
Generosity for Life digital philanthropy data platform
cards.fit_reason: Strong theme match, prominent philanthropy research role, and verified keynote and presentation experience.

cards.name: Pamala Wiepking
cards.job_title: Associate Professor of Philanthropic Studies; Stead Family Chair in International Philanthropy
cards.organization: Indiana University Lilly Family School of Philanthropy
cards.could_speak_on: How cross-national evidence and broader definitions of giving can inform the next era of philanthropic practice and funding.
talk_ideas: Understanding global generosity across contexts
How definitions and measurement shape global philanthropy research
What comparative research can teach funders about giving
cards.bio: Pamala Wiepking is an Associate Professor of Philanthropic Studies and the Stead Family Chair in International Philanthropy at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. Her research examines cross-national and interdisciplinary explanations of philanthropy, and her professional site describes keynote and workshop presentation offerings.
credentials: PhD
cards.why_fit: She brings a comparative research lens to questions about how philanthropic practices and institutions may evolve, and her own site identifies her as available for keynote presentations.

past_speaking.event: European Research Network of Philanthropy conference keynote lecture, Basel
Science of Philanthropy Initiative Conference 2026
Philanthropisms interview on understanding global generosity

notable_work: The Global Study of Philanthropy
Research on cross-national giving and volunteering
cards.fit_reason: Direct philanthropy scholarship and confirmed keynote experience; particularly strong for an evidence-based, global perspective.

cards.name: Alan J. Abramson
cards.job_title: Professor of Government and Politics; Founding Director, Center on Nonprofits, Philanthropy, and Social Enterprise
cards.organization: George Mason University, Schar School of Policy and Government
cards.could_speak_on: How nonprofit-government relationships, philanthropic institutions, and social enterprise shape the future of funding and public problem-solving.
talk_ideas: The changing relationship between nonprofits and government
Philanthropy and nonprofit-sector research: implications for funders
Social enterprise and collaborative governance
cards.bio: Alan J. Abramson is a professor at George Mason University’s Schar School of Policy and Government and founding director of its Center on Nonprofits, Philanthropy, and Social Enterprise. His work includes nonprofit and philanthropic issues, and his background includes nonprofit-sector research and public policy.
credentials: PhD in Political Science, Yale University
cards.why_fit: A senior scholar of nonprofits and philanthropy who can connect research with government and institutional perspectives relevant to the future of funding.

past_speaking.event: ARNOVA Annual Conference 2025 sessions

notable_work: Founding director of George Mason’s Center on Nonprofits, Philanthropy, and Social Enterprise
Research and work with leaders on nonprofit and philanthropic issues
cards.fit_reason: Strong subject-matter alignment and confirmed current academic role, though the verified speaking record is less extensive than the top-ranked candidates.

cards.name: Mirae Kim
cards.job_title: Professor, Schar School of Policy and Government
cards.could_speak_on: How nonprofit financial conditions, advocacy, and government engagement affect which organizations and communities philanthropy can support.
talk_ideas: What nonprofit trend data can tell funders about sector needs
Nonprofit advocacy and civic engagement in changing funding environments
Nonprofit financial management and philanthropic support
cards.bio: Mirae Kim is a professor at George Mason University’s Schar School of Policy and Government. Her research includes nonprofit financial management, advocacy and lobbying, arts management, and nonprofit contributions to racial and ethnic diversity; she leads the Nonprofit Organization Research Panel.
credentials: PhD in Public Affairs, Rutgers University
cards.why_fit: Her research offers an empirical view of nonprofit finances, advocacy, and government engagement—the organizational conditions that shape philanthropy’s impact.

past_speaking.event: ARNOVA Annual Conference panel: Engaged Nonprofit Scholarship
ARNOVA Annual Conference panel: Translating “Nonprofit”
ARNOVA Annual Conference panel: Nonprofits in the Crosshairs

notable_work: Leads the Nonprofit Organization Research Panel
National Survey of Nonprofit Trends and Impacts
Research on nonprofit advocacy and civic engagement

links.label: Mirae Kim personal and research profile

cards.fit_reason: A strong research fit for panels on nonprofit capacity and funding conditions, but less clearly established as a solo keynote draw.

cards.name: John Palfrey
cards.organization: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
cards.could_speak_on: How major foundations can use long-term grantmaking and collaborative initiatives to shape the next era of philanthropy.
talk_ideas: Philanthropy for what’s next: funding social change amid uncertainty
Building cross-sector initiatives to strengthen local journalism
Technology, information access, and the future of philanthropy
cards.bio: John Palfrey is president of the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation, which supports work across areas including climate solutions, criminal justice, and local news. He is an educator, author, legal scholar, and innovator with experience across education, nonprofit, and philanthropic sectors.
credentials: Author of 10 books, as author, co-author, or editor
cards.why_fit: A current leader of a major national foundation with directly relevant experience and a documented record of public talks on philanthropy; a strong fit for a national keynote audience.

past_speaking.event: Morton-Kenney Public Affairs Lecture, Southern Illinois University
Milken Institute Global Conference 2026 speaker
Philanthropy Massachusetts 57th Annual Conference keynote announcement

notable_work: Leads the MacArthur Foundation
Leads Press Forward, an initiative to strengthen local news organizations across the U.S.
cards.fit_reason: He leads a major philanthropy and has publicly addressed philanthropic challenges and sector-wide initiatives, with multiple speaking appearances confirmed.

cards.name: Amber D. Miller
cards.could_speak_on: How a large foundation can connect grantmaking with partners addressing climate change and the future of democratic, economic, and educational systems.
talk_ideas: Leading a foundation through complex, interconnected challenges
Bringing academic expertise into partnership with civic and business leaders
Funding responses to climate and democratic challenges
cards.bio: Amber D. Miller is president of the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, overseeing its grantmaking and work with grantee organizations. Before joining the foundation, she was dean of USC Dornsife College and the inaugural dean of science at Columbia University.
credentials: Ph.D. in physics, Princeton University
Fellow of the American Physical Society
cards.why_fit: As the head of a major grantmaking foundation, she offers a relevant practitioner perspective on how funders work with partners across complex societal issues. The pages checked confirmed her role but did not establish prior speaking appearances.
cards.fit_reason: A current foundation president with substantial organizational leadership experience; confirmed speaking history was not found in the pages checked.

dropped.name: Heather Gerken
dropped.reason: The evidence confirms she became Ford Foundation president in November 2025, but her professional background is primarily as a constitutional law scholar and academic. Under this practitioner-only category, she is better suited to the academic or policy category.

cards.name: Aaron Dorfman
cards.could_speak_on: How philanthropy can be more accountable and responsive to communities with less wealth, opportunity, and power.
talk_ideas: Who philanthropy serves: accountability to communities with less wealth and power
The role of grantmakers in supporting movements and civic engagement
Putting equity and responsiveness into philanthropic practice
cards.bio: Aaron Dorfman is president and CEO of NCRP, a research and advocacy organization focused on making grantmakers and wealthy donors more responsive to communities with less wealth, opportunity, and power. He frequently speaks and writes about philanthropy and equity, and serves on Georgetown University's Executive Certificate in Philanthropic Leadership faculty.
credentials: Philanthropic studies, Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University
cards.why_fit: He has led a national philanthropy accountability organization and has delivered a commencement address as well as remarks at the Yale Philanthropy Conference, making his perspective directly relevant to the conference theme.

past_speaking.event: Yale Philanthropy Conference
Commencement address, Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, Indiana University

notable_work: NCRP work on philanthropic responsiveness and accountability
cards.fit_reason: Directly aligned with philanthropic accountability and has prior speaking experience at Yale’s conference.

cards.name: Laura Tomasko
cards.job_title: Senior Policy Program Manager; Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy Practice Area Lead
cards.could_speak_on: How public policy, charitable giving, and impact investing are shaping the changing philanthropic landscape.
talk_ideas: Philanthropy and policy capacity: what data can reveal about sector change
Charitable giving during turbulent times
Impact investing and the evolving philanthropic toolkit
cards.bio: Laura Tomasko is a senior policy program manager and practice area lead at the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. Her work focuses on charitable giving, the philanthropic sector, and impact investing; she previously served in federal policy roles and worked with national philanthropy associations and community-based organizations.
credentials: MPA, Maxwell School
cards.why_fit: Her experience spans philanthropy, public policy, and federal government, and she moderated an Urban Institute summit session on charitable giving and philanthropy during turbulent times.

past_speaking.event: Giving Innovation Summit 2026: Charitable Giving and Philanthropy in Turbulent Times

cards.fit_reason: Offers a strong policy-and-sector perspective and demonstrated event moderation, though the verified speaking record here is limited to one event.

cards.name: Benjamin Soskis
cards.organization: Urban Institute, Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy
cards.could_speak_on: How philanthropy’s history can illuminate its present relationship to democratic norms and future practice.
talk_ideas: What philanthropy’s history can teach the sector about its future
Philanthropy, associational life, and democratic norms
Historical perspectives on charitable causes and donor priorities
cards.bio: Benjamin Soskis is a senior research associate in the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. His work explores how historical inquiry can inform contemporary philanthropic practice, and he holds a PhD in American history from Columbia University.
credentials: PhD in American history, Columbia University
cards.why_fit: He brings a distinctive historical lens to questions about philanthropy’s evolving role and its relationship to democratic life; the reviewed sources confirmed his expertise but did not verify a prior speaking appearance.
cards.fit_reason: A strong intellectual fit for the future-of-philanthropy theme, but no past speaking event was verified in the pages reviewed.

cards.name: Lori Villarosa

Previously served as a program officer at the Mott Foundation
cards.why_fit: Her work directly addresses how philanthropic institutions allocate resources, change grantmaking practice, and respond to community-led racial justice movements—an apt lens on who is shaping philanthropy’s future.

events.message: Reading your brief and planning the search…

Plan ready: Find nationally recognized philanthropy leaders suited to a keynote on who is shaping philanthropy’s future, prioritizing people with documented conference or public presentation experience. Medium budget favors established experts and select headliners; New Haven is the event location, but the search can be national.
Found 3 candidates (7 web searches): Heather Gerken, John Palfrey, Amber D. Miller
Found 1 candidates (6 web searches): Lori Villarosa
Found 3 candidates (6 web searches): David Callahan, Stacy Palmer, Andrew Simon
Found 3 candidates (10 web searches): Jeff Skoll, Alex Wilson, Pat Duffy
Found 3 candidates (9 web searches): Aaron Dorfman, Benjamin Soskis, Laura Tomasko
Found 4 candidates (9 web searches): Alan J. Abramson, Mirae Kim, Pamala Wiepking, Una Osili
Looking for people who would make great panels together…
Suggested 3 panel(s): The Future We Fund; Trust, Power, and the Donor Era; Giving’s Next Infrastructure

panels.title: The Future We Fund
panels.question: Who is shaping philanthropy’s next era, and how can funders respond to changing patterns of giving and public need?

members.name: Una Osili
members.angle: She brings research on demographic shifts, social norms, and global giving patterns.

members.name: John Palfrey
members.angle: He offers a major-foundation perspective on long-term grantmaking and collaborative initiatives.

members.name: Aaron Dorfman
members.angle: He focuses on making philanthropy more accountable and responsive to communities with less wealth and power.

members.name: Jeff Skoll
members.angle: He brings an entrepreneur-investor perspective on combining philanthropic capital, investment, and social enterprise.

moderator.name: Stacy Palmer
moderator.angle: She can guide a discussion of donor priorities, public trust, and accountability through her philanthropy reporting perspective.

why_together: They connect giving trends and research with the practical choices of major foundations, entrepreneurs, and accountability advocates.
Their approaches invite discussion of who sets philanthropic priorities and how funding can advance social change.
The group can weigh long-term institutional grantmaking alongside entrepreneurial and community-responsive approaches.
panels.tension: The panel can respectfully examine the balance between donor-led or entrepreneurial strategies and stronger accountability to the communities philanthropy aims to serve.
panels.balance_note: A cross-sector mix of academic, foundation, advocacy, and founder perspectives, moderated by a philanthropy journalist; all panelists have keynote or speaking experience reflected in their cards.

panels.title: Trust, Power, and the Donor Era
panels.question: As philanthropic power and donor priorities change, what can make giving more trusted, accountable, and responsive?

members.name: David Callahan
members.angle: He covers how mega-donors and their heirs are changing philanthropic power, priorities, and foundation models.

members.name: Lori Villarosa
members.angle: She brings a movement-informed perspective on racial-justice grantmaking, community accountability, and power-sharing.

members.name: Alan J. Abramson
members.angle: He connects philanthropy and nonprofit research with nonprofit-government relationships and public problem-solving.

members.name: Mirae Kim
members.angle: She brings evidence on nonprofit finances, advocacy, and government engagement that can inform funding decisions.

moderator.name: Stacy Palmer
moderator.angle: She can steer the conversation toward public trust and accountability, drawing on her philanthropy reporting perspective.

why_together: The panel connects changing donor power with the organizations and communities affected by funding decisions.
Research on nonprofit finances and government ties can ground the discussion of accountability in sector conditions.
Lori Villarosa’s movement-led lens creates a useful counterpoint to donor-centered accounts of philanthropy’s future.
panels.tension: The group can explore the tension between concentrated donor discretion and calls for philanthropy to share power and respond to community priorities.
panels.balance_note: Journalism, advocacy, and academic research meet in a discussion grounded in both philanthropic power and nonprofit realities.
shared_stage: Alan J. Abramson and Mirae Kim both appeared at: ARNOVA Annual Conference 2025 sessions

panels.title: Giving’s Next Infrastructure
panels.question: What new funding models and evidence will shape how philanthropy works in a changing world?

members.name: Pamala Wiepking
members.angle: She brings cross-national research on generosity and how definitions and measurement shape philanthropy.

members.name: Laura Tomasko
members.angle: She connects policy, sector data, charitable giving, and impact investing.

members.name: Alex Wilson
members.angle: He brings a platform-builder’s perspective on crypto philanthropy and emerging payment infrastructure.

members.name: Pat Duffy
members.angle: He focuses on how crypto fundraising tools and donor platforms can affect nonprofit revenue strategies.

moderator.name: Andrew Simon
moderator.angle: He can moderate from a journalism perspective on how philanthropic funding intersects with news and community priorities.

why_together: The panel links evidence about giving across contexts with policy and emerging fundraising infrastructure.
It brings nonprofit revenue questions into a discussion of new payment tools and philanthropic practice.
The mix can test technological optimism against the need for reliable evidence and useful sector-wide approaches.
panels.tension: The conversation can weigh the potential of new payment rails against questions about whether they offer broadly useful, evidence-informed ways to fund nonprofits.
panels.balance_note: Comparative philanthropy research and policy analysis meet two founders focused on digital fundraising tools, with a journalist moderating.
